newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares fall again, Kabo sale goes through.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares fall again, Kabo sale goes through.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell again on Wednesday, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) report said.
"Investors are still afraid this might not be the bottom and are reluctant to buy," said Rania Afifi of Intercapital brokerage. "Blue chips are attracting most of the trade."

The CMA overall index shed 0.65 points to 357.18 in trade worth 236.52 million pounds ($70 million), swollen by the state's sale of 196.86 million pounds' worth of shares in partially privatised Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles.
The state sold about 63 percent, 1.93 million shares, of the firm at 102 pounds a share, the minimum bid price in the auction. The stock, however, ended 0.25 lower at 101.75.

"When part of the firm was privatised in 1994, people then hoped it would be wholly sold because it is a good firm. But when this didn't materialise they were disappointed," said Ghada Sultan of EFG/Hermes brokerage.

Commercial International Bank (CIB), the most active on the day, closed 0.20 pounds higher at 73 after trade worth 3.7 million pounds. "People are used to buying CIB shares and then selling them after a couple of days or so at a profit," said Afifi.

Pyramids Breweries peroformed well, rising 5.45 pounds to 115.7. Brokers have attributed the price increase to a strong performance in the brewing company's London-listed Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs).
Most cements ended either unchanged or down. The most active among them, Amriyah Cement, closed a tiny 0.01 pound up at 84 in 3.43 million pounds of trade.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement remained unchanged at 88 pounds when shares worth 3.1 million changed hands.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 497.97 points from 498.19 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also fell to 261.78 from 262.45.
Out of the 80 shares traded, 25 rose, 31 fell while 24 ended unchanged.
